Content: Extended council-style repository audit campaign on audit/skeleton-animation-improvements-2026-09-07. Reviewed the repo council skill and used independent simulated seats because no independently invokable /council subagent was exposed. More than 390 explicitly numbered rounds plus additional distinct micro-rounds were performed across runtime generation, editor workflow, serialization, validation/sequencing, skeleton/IK, API ownership, resource lifetime, concurrency, numeric policy, compatibility/migration, performance, determinism, and adversarial equivalence. The campaign intentionally suppressed stale findings and duplicate task creation. Confirmed/fixed: generated-output collection and nested influence ownership, material-region input ownership, GeneratedCreatureData color ownership, clone-policy consolidation, one-resolution radius bridge, AppearanceBaker null contracts, MaterialRegion integer-overflow validation, SDF temp-buffer exception disposal, non-repairing CapsuleAxis canonicalization, NormalizeOr invalid-fallback contract, skeleton queue simplification, and preview component ownership hardening. Confirmed/tracked: TSK-0156 mutable Bone/Skeleton model; TSK-0159 mutable CreaturePart elements retained by hierarchy index; TSK-0154 broader GeneratedCreatureData ownership across async publication; TSK-0160 malformed MeshExtractionResult operations; TSK-0162 source fix awaiting validation; TSK-0163 BodyFrame default handedness mismatch; TSK-0164 JSON writer control-character escaping mismatch; TSK-0165 Unity-native Gradient/AnimationCurve evaluation from background Task.Run; TSK-0056 post-quantization key collisions; TSK-0095 snapshot/stage ownership umbrella. A subsequent branch-state review found duplicate task keys in the imported task directory: TSK-0166, TSK-0167, and TSK-0168 each had multiple independent records. The duplicate records were safely renumbered as TSK-0170 through TSK-0173 while preserving the earlier stable keys, and TSK-0169 references were updated to the renumbered TSK-0172 skinning-smear investigation. TSK-0169's editor skinning sweep implementation is now tracked as InProgress pending Unity validation. Continue treating task id/key uniqueness as a hard invariant. Do not blanket-convert Unity authoring palette Entries to immutable APIs. No Unity execution was performed; no new test is claimed as passing in Unity. Branch remains the working feature branch.
Conflicts: Older audits may still describe backing-list leaks, duplicate resolution paths, shallow GeneratedCreatureData colors, or the old canonicalizer CapsuleAxis repair; those findings are stale where current source now fixes them.

The repository task-tracker skill calls for MemorySmith MCP actions; that connector was unavailable here, so repository JSON was used as the existing fallback and remains subject to later MemorySmith reconciliation.

Task IDs must remain unique even when multiple agents/audit passes create closely related records; preserve the earliest stable key and renumber later independent records rather than silently keeping duplicate keys.
